recipes.name: Slow Cooker BBQ Chicken
ingredients_raw: 4 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves
2 dashes hot pepper sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Place chicken breasts into the bottom of a slow cooker.
In a bowl, stir together ketchup, maple syrup, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, chili powder, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, and hot sauce until mixture is well blended. Pour over chicken.
Cook on Low for 6 hours. Shred chicken with 2 forks, then cook for 30 more minutes. Serve shredded chicken and sauce spooned into sandwich rolls.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker BBQ Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker pulled chicken recipe features a from-scratch barbecue sauce sweetened with maple syrup for delicious shredded meat sandwiches.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I reduce the maple syrup to 1/4 cup and add 1/4 cup of Sweet Baby Ray's Hickory and Brown Sugar BBQ sauce for a little bit of smokiness.

My family LOVED this and it was so easy to make. I cut it down to 1/4c maple syrup and added 1/4c bbq sauce (I used Diana’s Honey BBQ). I used half the amount of chicken (2 large chicken breasts cut in half), but made the full amount of sauce. Using half the sauce, cooked for 5hrs on low, added the rest of the sauce, cooked on low for another 30mins. Shredded the chicken and served on toasted kaisers with grated old cheddar and thinly sliced avocado. So delish!

I sautéed onions, mushrooms and fresh garlic in my slow cooker prior to adding my chicken. Following another review, I reduced the 1/2 cup maple syrup to 1/4 maple syrup and added 1/4 cup Sweet Baby Ray’s Honey Barbecue sauce. I also eliminated the pepper seasonings. It’s not about making it spicy and hot. The recipe already had a good mix of liquid ingredients.

Very tasty! I followed other reviewers suggestions and replaced the maple syrup with 1/4 cup light brown sugar and 1/4 cup Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce. I used 2 T of regular, prepared yellow mustard and that was fine. (I was not sure if the recipe was calling for ground/powdered mustard or prepared mustard.) I also sliced up 1/2 a large onion and spread the slices over the chicken, but under the sauce. I used 2 - 1# each chicken breasts. Cooked everything in the slow cooker for 6 hours, pulled the chicken, and left it in the slow cooker for another 30 minutes. It was perfect. Everyone in the family loved this. I will definitely be making this again. So easy for a weeknight meal!

The kids loved this. I more than doubled it and I'm glad I did so we had leftovers for lunch. I didn't have the time so I cooked it on high for 2 hours and low for 1 hour and it turned out great. I did not add all the maple syrup and used some bbq sauce instead. I also didn't serve it on buns but I will do that next time.

So easy and so good! BF made himself one and then went back and made a 2nd because it was so good. I did cut the maple syrup in half as suggested. I cooked on high for 2.5 hours, then shredded and cooked another 30 minutes. I'd probably try 2 hours next time as I think the chicken was a little overcooked. 3 breasts for the amount of sauce seemed to work out perfectly.

Good, easy recipe. I used honey instead of maple syrup. I found the sauce a little too sweet for my liking, so when I made the second batch as suggested by the recipe, I used more of the Worcestershire sauce and the spicy ingredients. Put the two batches together and the sauce was just right!
Swapped out the ketchup for bbq sauce, and added 1/4 c of Frank’s Hot Sauce, and it’s just perfect

After reading some of the reviews, I was a little hesitant to put that much maple syrup into the recipe, as I typically prefer tangy to sweet. However my daughter doesn't like tangy or spicy, so I went ahead and gave it a try.
SO GLAD I DID!! 
I'm not sure why some reviewers said this doesn't taste like barbecue sauce. It's much more authentic tasting than majority of your name brand bottles, and was absolutely delicious! I have already made it twice, and swear I could live off of this stuff if it wasn't so expensive to make (using organic maple syrup, etc).
I did add onion powder to my sauce, and a dash of chipotle powder to give my sauce a bit of a smoky hint to it, but aside from that the only changes I made were cooking it for 5 1/2 hours the second time made, and I made a little more sauce. There is no need to double it, but make about a 1.5 batch, and that's just perfect! =)
Thank you so much for the awesome recipe!

Substituted some maple syrup (I used less than half of what was stated in the recipe) for BBQ sauce as I don't particularly have a sweet tooth. Also added a lot more hot sauce than described. Cooked for 4 hours on high, shredded the chicken, then left for another half an hour on high - simply due to time constraints. Also used tortilla wraps instead! Great recipe overall, only tweaks were down to personal preference.

We all really liked this! We used boneless chicken breasts. I took the suggestions and cut the maple syrup back to 1/4 c. I also added some liquid smoke. After shredding the chicken, I added it back to the slow cooker and mixed in some bottled barbeque sauce. Super easy!
"Make it again!", they said. So I will!
I didn't have any chili powder so I used paprika instead. Turned out beautifully.
Yum!! Perfect!
Very good. The barbecue sauce is exceptional. Had to leave out hot sauce as my wife can’t eat spicy. Don’t tell her the cayenne was in there. Didn’t need the full cook time. Plenty left for later.
Very good! Followed the recommendations & cut syrup in half & added bbq sauce! Will make again!
This was wonderful! I used pork ribs and slow baked them! I can see using most any meat would be successful as the sauce is perfect. Thank you for sharing.

Given that I was cooking for adults, I doubled the garlic and cayenne pepper spices. I also followed the suggestion of less maple syrup and adding barbecue sauce. The recipe was easy to make, and we enjoyed our dinner. We have some leftovers which should be even more delicious tomorrow.
We liked it. Will make again.
Very tasty! I used a habanero infused maple syrup and no cayenne pepper. I also added double the garlic and some onion powder.
